name: citeproof
description: Looks up scholarly citations from a pasted draft in Crossref, DataCite, OpenAlex and doi.org, reports references it could not find or whose DOI appears to point to a different paper, and quotes abstract sentences that may relate to a claim.

interface.longDescription: Paste a draft or reference list and Citeproof looks up each citation in Crossref, DataCite, OpenAlex and doi.org. It shows the closest matching record, a confidence score and any problems it detects, such as a DOI that appears to point to a different paper, a year that differs, a work marked as retracted in OpenAlex, or a reference it could not find. For a claim and a paper, it quotes abstract sentences that may relate to the claim and notes numbers from the claim that do not appear in the abstract. Limitations: scholarly works only (not case law or web pages); evidence is based on abstracts, not full text; "not found" means the work isn't in these indexes, which is not proof it doesn't exist. Citeproof reports only what these sources return; it cannot prove that a source is correct or that it supports a claim.
capabilities: Quote abstract sentences for a claim
defaultPrompt: Look up the references in my draft.
Does this DOI match my citation?
What does this paper's abstract say about my claim?

positive.description: Batch-check a bibliography that contains an entry that can't be verified
positive.prompt:
Check these references:
1. LeCun, Y., Bengio, Y., & Hinton, G. (2015). Deep learning. Nature, 521, 436–444. https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14539
2. Vaswani, A., et al. (2017). Attention is all you need. arXiv:1706.03762
3. Thompson, R., & Reyes, M. (2021). Neural correlates of citation hallucination in large language models. Journal of Cognitive Computing and AI, 14(3), 288–301. https://doi.org/10.5555/jcca.2021.14288
positive.expected_behavior: A table with one row per reference. 1 and 2 are verified with their DOIs. 3 is reported as not found: its DOI isn't registered with any DOI agency and no matching record exists. It is described only as not found / could not be verified, and no replacement citation is invented.

positive.description: Detect a DOI that points to a different paper
positive.prompt: Is this citation right? LeCun, Y., Bengio, Y., & Hinton, G. (2015). Deep learning. Nature, 521, 436–444. https://doi.org/10.1038/nature16961
positive.expected_behavior: Says the DOI resolves to a different work ('Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search', 2016) and that the cited paper matches 10.1038/nature14539.

positive.description: Find the DOI for a reference that has none
positive.prompt: Find the DOI for: He, Zhang, Ren, Sun (2016). Deep residual learning for image recognition. CVPR.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the matched record 10.1109/CVPR.2016.90 with its confidence and source, and shows the matched title, authors and year.

positive.description: Quote abstract evidence for a claim and flag a number the abstract doesn't contain
positive.prompt: Does the paper 10.1056/NEJMoa2034577 say the vaccine was 99% effective?
positive.expected_behavior: Quotes the most relevant abstract sentences verbatim (including the one stating 95% efficacy), notes that '99%' does not appear in the abstract, and gives no true/false verdict beyond the quoted text.

positive.description: Signed-in account: check a reference and export it as BibTeX in one call (uses the provided demo account)
positive.prompt: Check this reference and then export the result as BibTeX: Watson, J. D., & Crick, F. H. C. (1953). Molecular structure of nucleic acids. Nature, 171, 737–738.
positive.expected_behavior: After sign-in with the demo account, check_citations is called once with export_format "bibtex": the reference is verified (10.1038/171737a0) and the returned BibTeX entry for it is shown in the same reply. Unverified references would appear only as comments.

negative.prompt: Write me a literature review on sleep and memory with 10 APA references.

negative.description: General fact-checking with no paper or citation supplied
negative.prompt: Is it true that coffee causes cancer?

negative.description: Citation formatting is native ChatGPT functionality
negative.prompt: Convert my references from APA to MLA.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell anything or start any purchase. Every plugin feature, including exports (after sign-in), works without any purchase. When a usage limit is reached, the plugin states the limit and the reset time only.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: batch citation lookups, single-citation lookup, abstract quotes related to a claim, usage info, and exports for signed-in accounts.
